clue.text: Actor playing W. Churchill on the radio loots bank

parts.note: Gary Oldman played Winston Churchill in the film Darkest Hour; his initial and surname run together

indicators.note: something heard on the radio reaches us as sound only, so the spelling of the next word is not what counts

parts.note: to sack a town is to loot it

explanation.surface: A broadcast impersonation of Churchill turns into a story about a bank robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: G. OLDMAN, initial plus surname, makes the first word; the investment bank's second name is said exactly like SACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: The firm is a major American investment banking company, so it is one example of a bank.

clue.text: Regular servings of iced gin, rum, and spirits

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the word beside it is jumbled
servings handed out at regular intervals mean every other letter is taken

parts.note: first and third letters of iced
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bar list of iced gin, rum and other spirits served regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like another drink on the list, but it is the adjective meaning odd, and spirits is the definition, not more alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Genies are magical beings of Arabian folklore, and this is their plural, a word for supernatural spirits.

clue.text: You can't save this cad poked by holy person roughly

indicators.note: something poked has another thing pushed into its middle, so the following pieces go inside

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible man, a cad
ST is the abbreviation for saint
CA, short for circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: A rogue gets jostled by a vaguely saintly figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A louse is an old-fashioned insult for a cad; the saint and the circa go in together, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless undertaking that cannot succeed is one nobody can rescue, so the definition describes it as unsalvageable.

clue.text: Christmas gift produced, we hear, for fabulous lady

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the words before it are judged by their sound

parts.note: myrrh was one of the Magi's gifts at the Nativity, and produced means made

explanation.surface: A seasonal present is unwrapped and turns out to be for a remarkable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous here means belonging to fable or legend, and the half-woman, half-fish sea creature is a legendary female.

clue.text: Big rival from e.g. Tyneside, footballer with tail up

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means earlier in the word, so the final letter is shifted a place towards the top

parts.note: Lionel Messi, the Argentinian footballer

explanation.surface: A northern footballer celebrates against a major rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of MESSI moves up one place, giving MESIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch-enemy or long-standing opponent is a common modern sense of the word, from the Greek goddess of retribution.

clue.text: Got off, needing appeal after call to dismiss case

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so dismissing it keeps only the inner letters

parts.note: the word call without its first and last letters
IT is sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A defendant walks free after an appeal and a ruling that throws the case out.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from the 1927 film It, whose star became the original 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to get off a bus or horse, and the past tense has the older form alongside alighted.

clue.text: Dressed with e.g. leather on top, refusing to change

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top places a piece first, above the other one

parts.note: leather is an example of animal skin
dressed as a wound is, bandaged

explanation.surface: Someone is kitted out in leather, perhaps a book in a leather binding.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is narrow-minded and set in their ways sticks rigidly to tradition and resists new ideas.

clue.text: One on the left of major road that's within reach

indicators.note: within says that the preceding piece sits inside the following word

parts.note: to reach a place is to come to it
the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone stands on the left-hand side of a motorway within reaching distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the left politically describes a socialist, and this is the slang label for a communist.

clue.text: Did traffic race north round centre of Bordeaux?

indicators.note: going north in a down entry means reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to dart is to race or dash

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so these letters run backwards too
the centre of a word is its middle letters only

parts.note: the two middle letters of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A driver speeds north through the middle of a French city, wondering about the traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to buy and sell goods, often illegally, so the past tense matches the swapped and dealt sense.

clue.text: Gruff noises made by crew member bagging tat

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside a bag, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
tat is slang for a tattoo, which is ink

explanation.surface: A sailor grunts gruffly while hauling cheap junk aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Tat looks like rubbish, but here it is short for tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs make short grunting sounds, which can fairly be called gruff.

clue.text: One intended to jog round area's left part

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a reminder is meant to jog the memory
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A would-be runner sets off round a district.
explanation.walkthrough: Jog suggests running, but it is the jogging of a memory.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over once the rest is taken away is the leftover portion, the rest of something.

clue.text: Criminal calumnies inspiring a possible sentence

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the word takes in another piece
criminal suggests something crooked or bent out of its proper shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Criminal slanders could earn the culprit a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' seems to be a court penalty, but it is grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical clause that can stand alone may serve as a complete sentence by itself, so it is potentially one.

clue.text: High grade given by teacher having retired

parts.note: A is the top mark
a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree

explanation.surface: A retired teacher still awards top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired suggests leaving work, but here it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire can mean to go to sleep for the night, so someone who has done so is lying in bed.

clue.text: Interpret late modernist writer

parts.note: late as in former, an ex-
Ezra Pound, the American modernist poet

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to make sense of a recently deceased modernist author.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out and explain the meaning of a text or theory in detail is to interpret it.

clue.text: It's made with fried veg in proper state — ace!

parts.note: prim means proper and correct
to aver is to state firmly
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A cook praises a dish of fried vegetables made in the correct manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta primavera is an Italian-American dish of pasta with lightly cooked spring vegetables.

clue.text: Loan needing to be paid? Day is checked

parts.note: a sub is a small advance of money
a bill due is one needing payment
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A borrower checks the date a repayment falls due.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked in the sense of held back or restrained: something quietened and brought under control.

clue.text: One scours great announcement to secure work

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so the other piece is clasped inside

parts.note: brill is British slang for brilliant, great
an ad, advertisement, announces a product
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A searcher hunts for a splendid notice offering a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Brill is chatty British slang; the work is held between the two halves of the great announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: This trademarked steel-wool kitchen pad is used for scrubbing pans clean, the thing that scours.

clue.text: Happy following reporter's accurate account

indicators.note: following puts the first piece after the second, reversing the order the words appear
a reporter here is a speaker, so the next word comes to us spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: accurate means right
feeling up is feeling happy

explanation.surface: A cheerful journalist files a faithful report.
explanation.walkthrough: Reporter suggests a journalist, fitting the surface, but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper or magazine article describing an event is a report or account of it.

clue.text: Obstacle in current social event for misfit

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river, blocking its flow
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't fit in becomes an obstacle at a fashionable party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in current' reads like 'fashionable', but it describes a river's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric, odd person who does not fit in is informally called this name.

clue.text: Tie end of burlap sack

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: last letter of burlap
to sack workers is to lay them off

explanation.surface: Someone ties up the end of a hessian sack.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlap is coarse hessian cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding match after scores are level is used to settle a tied result, so a tie-breaker contest.

clue.text: Bash bone and make a hole

parts.note: the shin bone is the tibia
to dig is to make a hole

explanation.surface: Someone hits a leg bone hard enough to break through.
explanation.walkthrough: Bash reads as a blow, but it is a slang word for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively party or celebration is informally called a bash, and both are casual terms for it.

clue.text: Extremely silent, given gag for a punishment

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of silent
to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: A prisoner who talks is gagged into total silence as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Gag looks like a silencing cloth, but it is the verb meaning to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: A term in prison is informally called this, the time served as a sentence.

clue.text: Maybe what one did at butcher's shop in US city

definitions.text: Maybe what one did at butcher's shop
definitions.meaning: one may have bought a joint of pork there: got some ham, read as two words
a nickname for New York City, also Batman's home

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as GOT HAM for the shopping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington Irving gave New York City this nickname, and comics later made it Batman's hometown.

clue.text: Current head of state always gracious

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of state
ay is an old word for ever, always

explanation.surface: A present monarch is described as perpetually courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: Gracious here is the exclamation, as in 'Good gracious!'
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild old-fashioned exclamations of surprise, so they swap as interjections.

clue.text: A little glower from cavalier in hasty retreat

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: flight is a hasty retreat
cavalier means offhand, airy

explanation.surface: A dashing horseman flees, scowling slightly as he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Glower wants to mean a scowl; here it is something that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: A small decorative electric bulb on a string is a tiny thing that glows, read as glow-er.

clue.text: Loudly drink up, holding a historical Russian jug

indicators.note: loudly attaches to drink to describe the noisy gulping sound, leaving up as the turnaround signal
in a down entry, up means reading from bottom to top
holding something keeps it inside

parts.note: to glug is to drink noisily
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy drinker finishes off a Russian jug.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug is slang for prison, not a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet network of forced-labour camps was a notorious prison system, and jug is slang for jail.

clue.text: One ruler or another receiving tips from maharishi

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, another ruler

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends

parts.note: first and last letters of maharishi

explanation.surface: A sovereign takes advice from a guru.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a standard abbreviation for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim prince or commander in the Middle East is a ruler of a state or region.

clue.text: Daughter leaves second-class cereal in dish

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a ream is 500 leaves of paper
B is the second grade
oat is a cereal

explanation.surface: A daughter walks out on a bowl of inferior breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like a verb of departure; it is the pages of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is informal for a very attractive person, as is this word for a romantic ideal.

clue.text: Old president advanced, making lively steps

parts.note: James K. Polk, US president 1845-49
A is the abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: An elderly president moves forward, stepping briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: This quick Bohemian couple dance is a sequence of lively dance moves.

clue.text: Fabled curative which may be plucked from lab?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a drink taken as a supposed hangover cure

definitions.text: which may be plucked from lab
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a lab is a Labrador, so this is fur pulled from a pet

explanation.walkthrough: Lab looks like a laboratory, where cures are made; it is a Labrador.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an alcoholic drink taken the morning after to ease a hangover, a folk remedy.
